items.ko: 그럼에도 불구하고
items.ex: It was raining; nevertheless, the match began on time.
items.exko: 비가 왔지만 그럼에도 경기는 제시간에 시작했어요.

items.ko: ~인 반면에
items.ex: Ben likes quiet places, whereas his sister loves crowds.
items.exko: 벤은 조용한 곳을 좋아하는 반면 그의 여동생은 사람 많은 곳을 좋아해요.

items.ko: 비록 ~이지만
items.ex: She accepted the job, albeit with some doubts.
items.exko: 그녀는 약간 의심스러웠지만 그 일을 받아들였어요.

items.ko: 그래도, 개의치 않고
items.ex: The weather was awful, but the team trained regardless.
items.exko: 날씨가 끔찍했지만 팀은 개의치 않고 훈련했어요.

items.good: Whoever finishes first will win a prize.
items.ko: 가장 먼저 끝내는 사람은 누구든 상을 받을 거예요.
bad: Whomever finishes first will win a prize.
Whoever finish first will win a prize.
Whoever he finishes first will win a prize.

cz.st: ___ finishes first will win a prize.

items.rule: whoever는 '~하는 사람은 누구든지'라는 뜻이에요. 절 안에서 주어 역할을 하므로 whomever가 아니라 whoever를 쓰고, 동사도 3인칭 단수(finishes)로 받아요.
items.hint: 누가 끝내는지를 말하는 절이에요. 그 절 안에서 이 말이 어떤 역할인지 살펴보세요.

items.good: You can invite whoever wants to come.
items.ko: 오고 싶어 하는 사람은 누구든 초대해도 좋아요.
bad: You can invite whomever wants to come.
You can invite whoever wanting to come.
You can invite whoever to wants come.

cz.st: You can invite ___ wants to come.

items.rule: invite의 목적어 자리에 있어도, 복합관계대명사가 이끄는 절 안에서 wants의 주어이면 whoever를 써요. whomever는 절 안에서 목적어일 때 쓰는 형태예요.

items.good: Whatever you decide to do, I will support you.
items.ko: 무엇을 하기로 결정하든 나는 당신을 응원할 거예요.
bad: What you decide to do, I will support you.
Whatever do you decide to do, I will support you.
Whatever you decide to do it, I will support you.

cz.st: ___ you decide to do, I will support you.

items.rule: whatever + 주어 + 동사는 '무엇을 ~하든'이라는 양보의 부사절이에요. 평서문 어순을 유지하고, do의 목적어 역할을 하므로 it을 또 쓰지 않아요.
items.hint: '무엇을'에 해당하는 말이 do의 목적어가 되는 구조예요.

items.good: Whichever route you take, you will reach the station in ten minutes.
items.ko: 어느 길로 가든 10분 안에 역에 도착할 거예요.
bad: Whichever route you take it, you will reach the station in ten minutes.
Whichever you route take, you will reach the station in ten minutes.
Which route you take, you will reach the station in ten minutes.

cz.st: ___ route you take, you will reach the station in ten minutes.

items.rule: whichever + 명사는 정해진 범위 안에서 '어느 ~을 ...하든'이라는 뜻이에요. take의 목적어가 이미 whichever route이므로 it을 다시 쓰지 않아요.
items.hint: 정해진 길 중에서 '어느 쪽이든'을 뜻하는 말이 필요해요.

items.good: Wherever you go, remember to call your parents.
items.ko: 어디에 가든 부모님께 전화하는 것을 잊지 마세요.
bad: Wherever do you go, remember to call your parents.
Wherever you go there, remember to call your parents.
Wherever you goes, remember to call your parents.

cz.st: ___ you go, remember to call your parents.

items.rule: wherever는 '어디에(서) ~하든'이라는 뜻의 복합관계부사예요. 이미 장소 부사 역할을 하므로 there를 덧붙이지 않고, 의문문 어순으로 바꾸지도 않아요.
items.hint: '어디든'이라는 장소의 뜻이에요.

items.good: Whenever it rains, the road near our house floods.
items.ko: 비가 올 때마다 우리 집 근처 도로는 물에 잠겨요.
bad: Whenever it will rain, the road near our house floods.
Whenever it rains, the road near our house flood.
Whenever rains it, the road near our house floods.

cz.st: ___ it rains, the road near our house floods.

items.rule: whenever는 '~할 때마다, 언제 ~하든'이라는 뜻이에요. 시간을 나타내는 부사절에서는 미래의 일도 현재시제(rains)로 나타내요.
items.hint: '~할 때마다'라는 시간의 뜻이에요.

items.good: However tired she was, she finished the report.
items.ko: 그녀는 아무리 피곤해도 보고서를 끝냈어요.
bad: However she was tired, she finished the report.
However tired was she, she finished the report.
However tiredly she was, she finished the report.

cz.st: ___ tired she was, she finished the report.

items.rule: however 바로 뒤에 형용사나 부사를 두고 그 뒤에 주어 + 동사를 쓰면 '아무리 ~해도'라는 뜻이에요. 'However + 형용사 + 주어 + 동사' 어순을 지켜요.
items.hint: 형용사가 however 바로 뒤에 붙는 구조예요.

items.good: However hard you try, you cannot change the past.
items.ko: 아무리 노력해도 과거를 바꿀 수는 없어요.
bad: However you try hard, you cannot change the past.
However hard do you try, you cannot change the past.
However hardly you try, you cannot change the past.

cz.st: However ___ you try, you cannot change the past.

items.rule: 'however + 형용사/부사 + 주어 + 동사'에서 hard는 '열심히'라는 부사예요. hardly는 '거의 ~않다'라는 다른 뜻이라 맞지 않아요.
items.hint: '열심히'라는 뜻의 부사가 필요해요.

items.good: No matter what happens, we will not give up.
items.ko: 무슨 일이 일어나도 우리는 포기하지 않을 거예요.
bad: No matter what it happens, we will not give up.
No matter that happens, we will not give up.
No matter what happens, we will not giving up.

cz.st: No matter ___ happens, we will not give up.

items.rule: no matter what은 whatever와 같이 '무엇이 ~하더라도'라는 양보를 나타내요. what이 happens의 주어이므로 it을 또 쓰지 않아요.
items.hint: '무슨 일이'가 happens의 주어가 돼요.

items.good: No matter how busy he is, he always helps his neighbors.
items.ko: 그는 아무리 바빠도 항상 이웃을 도와요.
bad: No matter how he is busy, he always helps his neighbors.
No matter what busy he is, he always helps his neighbors.
No matter how busily he is, he always helps his neighbors.

cz.st: No matter ___ busy he is, he always helps his neighbors.

items.rule: no matter how 뒤에는 형용사/부사를 바로 붙이고 '주어 + 동사'를 써요. be동사 뒤의 보어는 형용사(busy)이므로 부사 busily는 쓸 수 없어요.
items.hint: 정도를 나타내는 말이 형용사 busy 바로 앞에 와요.

items.good: No matter who you ask, the answer will be the same.
items.ko: 누구에게 물어도 대답은 같을 거예요.
bad: No matter who you ask it, the answer will be the same.
No matter that you ask, the answer will be the same.
No matter who do you ask, the answer will be the same.

cz.st: No matter ___ you ask, the answer will be the same.

items.rule: no matter who + 주어 + 동사는 '누구를 ~하더라도'라는 뜻이에요. 의문사처럼 보이지만 절 안에서는 평서문 어순(you ask)을 써요.
items.hint: '누구에게'에 해당하는 의문사가 필요해요.

items.good: No matter where you live, you can join our online club.
items.ko: 어디에 살든 우리 온라인 동아리에 가입할 수 있어요.
bad: No matter where do you live, you can join our online club.
No matter where you live there, you can join our online club.
No matter where you lives, you can join our online club.

cz.st: No matter ___ you live, you can join our online club.

items.rule: no matter where는 wherever와 같은 뜻이에요. where가 이미 장소를 나타내므로 there를 덧붙이지 않고, 주어 you에 맞춰 live를 써요.
items.hint: 장소를 나타내는 의문사가 필요해요.

items.good: Although it was raining, we went out for a walk.
items.ko: 비가 오고 있었지만 우리는 산책하러 나갔어요.
bad: Although it was raining, but we went out for a walk.
Despite it was raining, we went out for a walk.
Although raining it was, we went out for a walk.

cz.st: ___ it was raining, we went out for a walk.

items.rule: although는 접속사라서 뒤에 '주어 + 동사' 절이 와요. 한 문장에서 although와 but을 함께 쓰지 않아요. despite는 전치사라 절을 이끌 수 없어요.
items.hint: 뒤에 '주어 + 동사' 절이 이어지는 말이 필요해요.

items.good: Despite the heavy traffic, we arrived on time.
items.ko: 교통 체증이 심했는데도 우리는 제시간에 도착했어요.
bad: Despite the traffic was heavy, we arrived on time.
Although the heavy traffic, we arrived on time.
Despite of the heavy traffic, we arrived on time.

cz.st: ___ the heavy traffic, we arrived on time.

items.rule: despite는 전치사이므로 명사구(the heavy traffic)가 뒤따라요. 'despite of'라고 쓰지 않고, 절 앞에는 although를 써요.
items.hint: 뒤에 명사구만 오고 있어요.

items.good: In spite of being tired, she stayed up to help us.
items.ko: 그녀는 피곤했지만 우리를 도우려고 깨어 있었어요.
bad: In spite of she was tired, she stayed up to help us.
In spite being tired, she stayed up to help us.
In spite of been tired, she stayed up to help us.

cz.st: In spite of ___ tired, she stayed up to help us.

items.rule: in spite of는 전치사구이므로 뒤에 명사나 동명사(being)가 와요. 'in spite of + 주어 + 동사' 형태는 쓸 수 없어요.
items.hint: 전치사 뒤이므로 동사의 -ing 형태가 알맞아요.

items.good: Even though he is only twelve, he plays chess very well.
items.ko: 그는 겨우 열두 살인데도 체스를 아주 잘 둬요.
bad: Even though he is only twelve, but he plays chess very well.
Despite he is only twelve, he plays chess very well.
Even though he is only twelve, he play chess very well.

cz.st: ___ he is only twelve, he plays chess very well.

items.rule: even though는 although를 강조한 접속사로, 사실과 대비되는 내용을 '주어 + 동사' 절로 이끌어요. despite, in spite of, because of는 전치사(구)라 절을 이끌 수 없어요.
items.hint: 뒤에 '주어 + 동사' 절이 오므로 접속사가 필요해요.

items.good: Even if it snows tomorrow, the game will be held.
items.ko: 내일 눈이 오더라도 경기는 열릴 거예요.
bad: Even if it will snow tomorrow, the game will be held.
Even if it snowed tomorrow, the game will be held.
Even if it snows tomorrow, the game will be hold.

cz.st: Even ___ it snows tomorrow, the game will be held.

items.rule: even if는 '(설사) ~하더라도'라는 가정의 양보를 나타내요. 조건·양보의 부사절에서는 미래의 일도 현재시제(snows)로 쓰고, 수동태는 be + 과거분사(held)예요.
items.hint: 아직 일어나지 않은 일을 가정하는 말이에요.

items.good: While I understand your point, I cannot agree.
items.ko: 당신의 말은 이해하지만 동의할 수는 없어요.
bad: While I understand your point, but I cannot agree.
While I understanding your point, I cannot agree.
While I understand your point, I cannot to agree.

cz.st: ___ I understand your point, I cannot agree.

items.rule: 문장 앞의 while은 although처럼 '~이긴 하지만'이라는 양보의 뜻이에요. 절 앞에 오므로 전치사 despite, because of는 쓸 수 없어요.
items.hint: 뒤에 '주어 + 동사'가 오고 '~이긴 하지만'이라는 뜻이에요.

items.good: Some people prefer cities, whereas others like the countryside.
items.ko: 어떤 사람들은 도시를 선호하는 반면 다른 사람들은 시골을 좋아해요.
bad: Some people prefer cities, whereas others likes the countryside.
Some people prefer cities, whereas but others like the countryside.
Some people prefer cities, whereas of others like the countryside.

cz.st: Some people prefer cities, ___ others like the countryside.

items.rule: whereas는 두 가지를 대조하여 '~인 반면에'라는 뜻의 접속사예요. 뒤에 '주어 + 동사'가 오고, but 같은 다른 접속사를 겹쳐 쓰지 않아요.
items.hint: 두 집단을 대조하는 접속사가 필요해요.

items.good: Young as he is, he leads the team well.
items.ko: 그는 어리지만 팀을 잘 이끌어요.
bad: Young as is he, he leads the team well.
As young he is, he leads the team well.
Young as he is, but he leads the team well.

cz.st: Young ___ he is, he leads the team well.

items.rule: '형용사 + as + 주어 + 동사'는 '~이지만'이라는 뜻의 양보 구문이에요(Young though he is와 같은 뜻). 보어를 앞으로 내고 as를 써요.
items.hint: 형용사를 문장 앞으로 보내고 그 뒤에 접속사가 와요.

items.good: Try as she might, she could not open the old door.
items.ko: 아무리 애를 써도 그녀는 낡은 문을 열 수 없었어요.
bad: Try as might she, she could not open the old door.
Try as she might it, she could not open the old door.
Trying as she might, she could not open the old door.

cz.st: Try ___ she might, she could not open the old door.

items.rule: '동사원형 + as + 주어 + might/may'는 '아무리 ~하려 해도'라는 양보의 관용 구문이에요. 주어 she 뒤에 조동사 might가 바로 와요.
items.hint: 동사원형을 앞으로 낸 양보 구문이에요.

items.good: Whether you agree or not, you have to follow the rules.
items.ko: 동의하든 안 하든 규칙은 따라야 해요.
bad: Whether you agree and not, you have to follow the rules.
Whether you agree not, you have to follow the rules.
Whether you agree or not, you having to follow the rules.

cz.st: ___ you agree or not, you have to follow the rules.

items.rule: whether A or B는 '~이든 아니든'이라는 양보의 부사절이에요. whether와 짝이 되는 말은 or이고, 주절의 동사는 정상적인 형태(have to)로 써요.
items.hint: '~이든 아니든'이라는 뜻이에요.

items.good: Whoever you are, you must show your ticket.
items.ko: 당신이 누구든 표를 보여 주어야 해요.
bad: Whomever you are, you must show your ticket.
Whoever are you, you must show your ticket.
Whoever you are, you must to show your ticket.

cz.st: ___ you are, you must show your ticket.

items.rule: whoever you are에서 whoever는 be동사의 보어예요. 보어 자리에서 주어와 같은 사람을 가리킬 때는 whoever를 쓰고, 평서문 어순(you are)을 유지해요.
items.hint: be동사 뒤에 올 보어에 해당하는 말이에요.

items.good: The teacher gave a sticker to whoever answered the question correctly.
items.ko: 선생님은 그 질문에 정확히 답한 사람 누구에게나 스티커를 주었어요.
bad: The teacher gave a sticker to whomever answered the question correctly.
The teacher gave a sticker to whoever answer the question correctly.
The teacher gave a sticker to who answered the question correctly.

cz.st: The teacher gave a sticker to ___ answered the question correctly.

items.rule: 전치사 to 뒤라도 whoever 절 전체가 전치사의 목적어가 되고, 절 안에서 answered의 주어는 whoever예요. 그래서 whomever가 아니라 whoever를 써요.
items.hint: 전치사 뒤이지만, 뒤에 오는 절에서 주어 역할을 하는 말을 골라야 해요.

items.good: You may take whichever seat you prefer.
items.ko: 원하는 어느 좌석이든 앉아도 좋아요.
bad: You may take whichever seat you prefer it.
You may take whichever you seat prefer.
You may take whoever seat you prefer.

cz.st: You may take ___ seat you prefer.

items.rule: whichever + 명사는 '어느 ~이든'이라는 뜻의 복합관계형용사예요. 명사 seat을 꾸미므로 사람을 가리키는 whoever는 쓰지 않아요.
items.hint: 명사 seat 바로 앞에서 그것을 꾸며 줘요.

items.good: Choose whatever color you like best.
items.ko: 가장 마음에 드는 색이면 무엇이든 고르세요.
bad: Choose whatever color do you like best.
Choose whatever color you like it best.
Choose whenever color you like best.

cz.st: Choose ___ color you like best.

items.rule: whatever + 명사는 '어떤 ~이든'이라는 뜻이에요. 절 안은 평서문 어순이고, like의 목적어는 whatever color이므로 it을 쓰지 않아요.
items.hint: 명사 color를 꾸미는 말이에요.

items.good: We can meet whenever it is convenient for you.
items.ko: 당신이 편한 때라면 언제든 만날 수 있어요.
bad: We can meet whenever it are convenient for you.
We can meet whenever it convenient for you.
We can meet whenever of it is convenient for you.

cz.st: We can meet ___ it is convenient for you.

items.rule: whenever는 '~할 때는 언제든지'라는 뜻의 복합관계부사예요. 뒤에는 주어 it과 동사 is를 모두 갖춘 절이 와요.

items.good: He packs his camera wherever he travels.
items.ko: 그는 어디로 여행을 가든 카메라를 챙겨요.
bad: He packs his camera wherever he travels there.
He packs his camera whatever he travels.
He packs his camera wherever does he travel.

cz.st: He packs his camera ___ he travels.

items.rule: wherever는 '~하는 곳은 어디든'이라는 뜻이고 그 자체가 장소 부사 역할을 해요. there를 덧붙이거나 의문문 어순을 쓰지 않아요.

items.good: However much money you earn, you should save some of it.
items.ko: 돈을 아무리 많이 벌어도 일부는 저축해야 해요.
bad: However money much you earn, you should save some of it.
However many money you earn, you should save some of it.
However much money do you earn, you should save some of it.

cz.st: However ___ money you earn, you should save some of it.

items.rule: however much + 셀 수 없는 명사 + 주어 + 동사는 '~을 아무리 많이 ...해도'라는 뜻이에요. money는 셀 수 없는 명사라서 many가 아니라 much를 써요.
items.hint: money가 셀 수 있는 명사인지 생각해 보세요.

items.good: However many times I read it, I cannot remember the poem.
items.ko: 아무리 여러 번 읽어도 그 시를 기억할 수 없어요.
bad: However times many I read it, I cannot remember the poem.
However much times I read it, I cannot remember the poem.
However many times do I read it, I cannot remember the poem.

cz.st: However ___ times I read it, I cannot remember the poem.

items.rule: times처럼 셀 수 있는 복수 명사 앞에는 however many를 써요. however 바로 뒤에 many가 오고, 그 뒤에 명사가 따라와요.
items.hint: times는 셀 수 있는 복수형이에요.

items.good: Strange as it may seem, he never uses a phone.
items.ko: 이상하게 보일지 몰라도 그는 전화기를 전혀 쓰지 않아요.
bad: Strange as may it seem, he never uses a phone.
Strange as it may seems, he never uses a phone.
As strange it may seem, he never uses a phone.

cz.st: Strange ___ it may seem, he never uses a phone.

items.rule: '형용사 + as + 주어 + may/might + 동사'는 '~일지라도'라는 양보 구문이에요. may 뒤에는 동사원형(seem)이 와요.
items.hint: 형용사를 문장 앞에 둔 양보 구문이에요.

items.good: He finished the soup, though it was cold.
items.ko: 그는 수프가 식었지만 다 먹었어요.
bad: He finished the soup, though but it was cold.
He finished the soup, despite it was cold.
He finished the soup, though of it was cold.

cz.st: He finished the soup, ___ it was cold.

items.rule: though는 문장 끝쪽에서도 '~이지만'이라는 접속사로 쓰여 뒤에 '주어 + 동사' 절을 이끌어요. despite와 in spite of는 전치사(구)예요.

items.good: No matter how carefully I check, I always miss a small mistake.
items.ko: 아무리 꼼꼼히 확인해도 나는 항상 작은 실수를 놓쳐요.
bad: No matter how carefully do I check, I always miss a small mistake.
No matter how careful I check, I always miss a small mistake.
No matter how I carefully check, I always miss a small mistake.

cz.st: No matter how ___ I check, I always miss a small mistake.

items.rule: check는 일반동사이므로 이를 꾸미는 말은 부사(carefully)예요. 'no matter how + 부사 + 주어 + 동사' 어순을 지켜요.
items.hint: 동사 check를 꾸미는 품사를 생각해 보세요.

items.good: Whatever the weather is like, the festival will go on.
items.ko: 날씨가 어떻든 축제는 계속될 거예요.
bad: Whatever is the weather like, the festival will go on.
What the weather is like, the festival will go on.
Whatever the weather is like it, the festival will go on.

cz.st: ___ the weather is like, the festival will go on.

items.rule: whatever + 주어 + be동사 + like는 '(무엇이) ~와 같든'이라는 양보의 부사절이에요. what만 쓰면 양보의 뜻이 되지 않고, 절 안은 평서문 어순을 지켜요.
items.hint: '어떠하든'이라는 뜻의 양보절이에요.

items.good: Regardless of the cost, she bought the tickets.
items.ko: 비용에 상관없이 그녀는 표를 샀어요.
bad: Regardless the cost, she bought the tickets.
Regardless of the cost is, she bought the tickets.
Regardless that the cost, she bought the tickets.

cz.st: Regardless ___ the cost, she bought the tickets.

items.rule: regardless of는 '~에 상관없이'라는 뜻의 전치사구이고 뒤에 명사(구)가 와요. of를 빼거나 다른 전치사로 바꾸지 않아요.
items.hint: '~에 상관없이'라는 짝이 되는 전치사가 필요해요.

items.good: Regardless of how old you are, you can join the choir.
items.ko: 몇 살이든 상관없이 합창단에 들어올 수 있어요.
bad: Regardless of how old are you, you can join the choir.
Regardless of how you are old, you can join the choir.
Regardless of how old you are, you can to join the choir.

cz.st: Regardless of ___ old you are, you can join the choir.

items.rule: regardless of 뒤에는 'how + 형용사 + 주어 + 동사' 같은 명사절도 올 수 있어요. 간접의문문이므로 어순은 how old you are예요.
items.hint: '얼마나 나이가 들었든'이라는 정도를 묻는 말이에요.

items.good: Whatever may happen, I will keep my promise.
items.ko: 무슨 일이 일어나더라도 나는 약속을 지킬 거예요.
bad: Whatever may happens, I will keep my promise.
Whatever may it happen, I will keep my promise.
Whatever happen may, I will keep my promise.

cz.st: Whatever may ___, I will keep my promise.

items.rule: 양보절에서는 may를 써서 'Whatever may happen'이라고도 해요. 조동사 may 뒤에는 동사원형(happen)이 와요.
items.hint: 조동사 may 바로 뒤에 올 동사의 형태를 생각해 보세요.

items.good: Whichever team wins will play in the final.
items.ko: 이기는 팀은 어느 쪽이든 결승전에서 경기를 하게 돼요.
bad: Whichever team win will play in the final.
Whichever teams wins will play in the final.
Whichever team wins will to play in the final.

cz.st: ___ team wins will play in the final.

items.rule: Whichever team wins가 문장 전체의 주어 역할을 하는 명사절이에요. team이 단수이므로 동사는 wins이고, will 뒤에는 동사원형만 와요.

items.good: Whatever she cooks tastes wonderful.
items.ko: 그녀가 요리하는 것은 무엇이든 맛있어요.
bad: Whatever she cooks taste wonderful.
Whatever she cooks it tastes wonderful.
Whenever she cooks tastes wonderful.

cz.st: ___ she cooks tastes wonderful.

items.rule: 여기서 whatever she cooks는 '그녀가 요리하는 것은 무엇이든'이라는 뜻의 명사절로 문장의 주어예요. 주어가 하나뿐이므로 it을 또 쓰지 않고, 동사는 tastes예요.

items.good: Much as I like him, I cannot lend him any money.
items.ko: 그를 아무리 좋아해도 돈을 빌려줄 수는 없어요.
bad: Much I like him as, I cannot lend him any money.
Much as I like him, but I cannot lend him any money.
Much as I like him, I cannot to lend him any money.

cz.st: ___ as I like him, I cannot lend him any money.

items.rule: 'Much as + 주어 + 동사'는 '아무리 ~해도'라는 뜻이에요. like의 정도를 나타내는 부사 much를 앞으로 낸 형태이고, many는 셀 수 있는 명사에만 써요.
items.hint: 정도를 나타내는 부사를 앞으로 낸 구문이에요.

items.good: Whether we win or lose, we will have fun.
items.ko: 이기든 지든 우리는 즐거울 거예요.
bad: Whether we wins or lose, we will have fun.
Whether win we or lose, we will have fun.
Whether we win or lose, we will having fun.

cz.st: Whether we win ___ lose, we will have fun.

items.rule: whether A or B에서 or는 짝이 되는 말이에요. 양보의 whether절은 'Whether we win or lose'처럼 현재시제로 쓰는 것이 자연스럽고, 주어 we에는 win을 써요. 주절의 will 뒤에는 동사원형이 와요.
items.hint: whether와 짝이 되는 접속사를 떠올려 보세요.

items.good: Although tired, the runners kept going.
items.ko: 지쳤지만 달리는 사람들은 계속 나아갔어요.
bad: Although tired, kept going the runners.
Although tiring, the runners kept going.
Despite tired, the runners kept going.

cz.st: Although ___, the runners kept going.

items.rule: although 뒤에서 '주어 + be동사'를 생략하면 although tired처럼 형용사만 남을 수 있어요. 달리는 사람들이 '지친' 상태이므로 과거분사에서 온 형용사 tired를 써요.
items.hint: 사람의 상태를 나타내는 형용사가 필요해요.

items.good: Despite having little money, he gave generously.
items.ko: 그는 돈이 거의 없었는데도 아낌없이 베풀었어요.
bad: Despite have little money, he gave generously.
Despite of having little money, he gave generously.
Despite he had little money, he gave generously.

cz.st: Despite ___ little money, he gave generously.

items.rule: despite는 전치사이므로 뒤에 동명사(having)를 쓸 수 있어요. 동사원형이나 과거형, to부정사는 올 수 없어요.
items.hint: 전치사 뒤에 올 수 있는 동사의 형태를 떠올려 보세요.

items.good: Despite the fact that he was ill, he went to work.
items.ko: 그는 아팠다는 사실에도 불구하고 출근했어요.
bad: Despite that he was ill, he went to work.
Despite of the fact that he was ill, he went to work.
Despite the fact that he was ill, but he went to work.

cz.st: Despite the ___ that he was ill, he went to work.

items.rule: despite 뒤에 절을 쓰고 싶으면 'the fact that + 주어 + 동사'처럼 명사구로 만들어요. that 단독이나 of를 덧붙이는 것은 쓸 수 없어요.
items.hint: that절의 내용을 설명하는 명사가 필요해요.

items.good: There are two roads; take whichever you like.
items.ko: 길이 두 개 있으니 마음에 드는 쪽으로 가세요.
bad: There are two roads; take whichever you like it.
There are two roads; take whichever do you like.
There are two roads; take whoever you like.

cz.st: There are two roads; take ___ you like.

items.rule: 정해진 범위(두 길) 안에서 하나를 고를 때는 whichever를 써요. whoever와 whom은 사람을 가리키고, whichever 절 안에서 like의 목적어는 whichever예요.

items.good: No matter which dress she chooses, she looks elegant.
items.ko: 그녀는 어떤 드레스를 골라도 우아해 보여요.
bad: No matter which dress she chooses it, she looks elegant.
No matter which she chooses dress, she looks elegant.
No matter whichever dress she chooses, she looks elegant.

cz.st: No matter ___ dress she chooses, she looks elegant.

items.rule: no matter which + 명사는 '어느 ~을 ...하더라도'라는 뜻이에요. no matter 뒤에는 -ever 형태를 쓰지 않고 which, what, who, how 같은 의문사를 써요.
items.hint: no matter 뒤에 쓰는 의문사 형태를 떠올려 보세요.

items.good: However rich a person may be, he cannot buy time.
items.ko: 사람이 아무리 부유하더라도 시간을 살 수는 없어요.
bad: However rich may a person be, he cannot buy time.
However a person may be rich, he cannot buy time.
However richly a person may be, he cannot buy time.

cz.st: However ___ a person may be, he cannot buy time.

items.rule: however 뒤에는 보어 역할의 형용사를 바로 붙여요. may be 뒤의 보어는 형용사이므로 부사 richly나 명사형은 쓸 수 없어요.
items.hint: be동사의 보어로 쓰이는 품사를 생각해 보세요.

items.good: Whenever you are ready, we can start.
items.ko: 준비가 되면 언제든 시작할 수 있어요.
bad: Whenever you will be ready, we can start.
Whenever you ready, we can start.
Whenever are you ready, we can start.

cz.st: Whenever you ___ ready, we can start.

items.rule: 시간을 나타내는 whenever절에서는 미래의 일도 현재시제로 쓰고, 주어 you에는 are를 써요.
items.hint: 주어가 you일 때의 be동사와 시제를 확인해 보세요.

items.good: Wherever there is water, plants can grow.
items.ko: 물이 있는 곳이면 어디서든 식물이 자랄 수 있어요.
bad: Wherever it is water, plants can grow.
Wherever there are water, plants can grow.
Wherever has water, plants can grow.

cz.st: Wherever there ___ water, plants can grow.

items.rule: 'There is + 단수/셀 수 없는 명사'이므로 water 앞에는 is를 써요. wherever 뒤에도 there is 구문이 올 수 있어요.
items.hint: water가 셀 수 있는 명사인지 생각해 보세요.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은?
___ you say to me, I won't change my mind.
items.why: say의 목적어 역할을 하면서 '무엇을 ~하든'이라는 뜻이 필요하므로 whatever가 알맞아요.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은?
___ of the two buses you take, you will arrive before noon.
items.why: 두 대의 버스 중에서 고르는 상황이므로 '어느 쪽을 ~하든'이라는 뜻의 whichever가 알맞아요.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은?
___ hard we tried, we could not open the safe.
items.why: 형용사/부사 hard 앞에서 '아무리 ~해도'라는 뜻을 나타내는 말은 however예요.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은?
The match went on ___ the rain had not stopped.
items.why: 빈칸 뒤에 '주어 + 동사' 절이 있으므로 접속사 even though가 알맞아요. 나머지는 전치사(구)라서 절을 이끌 수 없어요.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은?
___ his poor health, my grandfather walks to the park every morning.
items.why: 빈칸 뒤에 명사구(his poor health)만 있으므로 전치사 despite가 알맞아요. 나머지는 절을 이끄는 접속사예요.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은?
Tom is quiet in class, ___ his sister talks to everyone.
items.why: 두 사람을 대조하는 문장이고 뒤에 절이 이어지므로 '~인 반면에'라는 whereas가 알맞아요.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은?
___ you are ready, we can leave.
items.why: '준비가 되면 언제든'이라는 시간의 뜻이므로 whenever가 알맞아요. 나머지는 are ready의 보어나 주어 자리에 맞지 않아요.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은?
You can eat ___ you find in the fridge.
items.why: eat의 목적어 역할을 하는 '~하는 것은 무엇이든'이라는 뜻이므로 whatever가 알맞아요.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은?
Please sit ___ you like. All the seats are free.
items.why: '앉고 싶은 곳은 어디든'이라는 장소의 뜻이므로 wherever가 알맞아요.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은?
Dress warmly, ___ the weather may be.
items.why: '날씨가 어떠하든'이라는 뜻의 양보절은 whatever the weather may be로 나타내요.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은?
___ our team wins or loses, we will cheer.
items.why: '이기든 지든'이라는 양보의 뜻은 whether ... or ...로 나타내요.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은?
She wore a coat ___ it was quite warm.
items.why: 따뜻한 날씨에도 코트를 입었다는 대조의 의미이므로 even though가 알맞아요.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은?
I will wait here, ___ long it takes.
items.why: '아무리 오래 걸려도'는 however long으로 나타내요.

items.q:
빈칸에 알맞은 말은?
___ the reason is, honesty is always the best choice.
items.why: '이유가 무엇이든'이라는 뜻이므로 whatever가 알맞아요.

items.q:
다음 문장에서 어법상 틀린 부분을 바르게 고친 것은?
Despite it was raining, we played soccer.
items.why: despite는 전치사라서 절을 이끌 수 없어요. 절 앞에는 접속사 although를 써야 해요.

items.q:
다음 문장에서 어법상 틀린 부분을 바르게 고친 것은?
Whomever finishes the test first may leave early.
items.why: finishes의 주어 역할을 하므로 whomever가 아니라 whoever를 써야 해요.

items.q:
다음 문장에서 어법상 틀린 부분을 바르게 고친 것은?
However I try hard, I cannot lift this rock.
o: However I try → Whatever I try
However I try hard → However hard I try
items.why: '아무리 열심히 해도'는 however 바로 뒤에 hard를 붙인 However hard I try 어순이에요.

items.q:
다음 문장에서 어법상 틀린 부분을 바르게 고친 것은?
No matter what do you choose, I will respect it.
o: what do you choose → what you choose
I will respect → I will respects
No matter what → No matters what
items.why: no matter what절 안에서는 의문문이 아닌 평서문 어순(you choose)을 써요.

items.q:
다음 문장에서 어법상 틀린 부분을 바르게 고친 것은?
In spite of he was ill, he joined the trip.
items.why: in spite of는 전치사구라 절을 이끌 수 없어요. 절 앞에서는 although를 써야 해요.

items.q:
다음 문장에서 어법상 틀린 부분을 바르게 고친 것은?
Whatever you decide it, I will go with you.
items.why: whatever가 이미 decide의 목적어이므로 it을 또 쓰면 안 돼요.

items.q:
다음 문장에서 though는 그대로 둘 때, 어법상 불필요한 단어는?
Though the road was long, but we enjoyed the walk.
items.why: though와 but은 함께 쓰지 않아요. 접속사 though가 있으므로 but을 빼야 해요.

items.q:
다음 문장에서 어법상 틀린 부분을 바르게 고친 것은?
Whoever are late will have to clean the room.
items.why: whoever절은 단수로 취급하므로 동사는 are가 아니라 is를 써요.

items.q:
다음 문장에서 어법상 틀린 부분을 바르게 고친 것은?
Whenever I will see her, I feel happy.
items.why: 시간을 나타내는 부사절에서는 미래의 일도 현재시제로 쓰므로 will see가 아니라 see예요.

items.q:
다음 문장에서 어법상 틀린 부분을 바르게 고친 것은?
Despite of the rain, the game went on.
items.why: despite는 그 자체가 전치사이므로 of를 붙이지 않아요. (in spite of는 of가 필요해요.)

items.q:
다음 문장에서 어법상 틀린 부분을 바르게 고친 것은?
However much does it cost, I will buy this bike.
items.why: however much절 안에서는 의문문 어순이 아니라 평서문 어순(it costs)을 써요.

items.q:
다음 문장에서 어법상 틀린 부분을 바르게 고친 것은?
Young as is he, he leads the team well.
o: as is he → as he is
items.why: 양보 구문 'Young as he is'에서 as 뒤는 '주어 + 동사' 어순이에요.

items.q: 'Whoever comes first will be served first.'에서 whoever와 바꿔 쓸 수 있는 말은?
items.why: whoever는 '~하는 사람은 누구든'이라는 뜻으로 anyone who와 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요. no matter who는 문장의 주어가 될 수 없어요.

items.q: 'No matter where she goes'와 같은 뜻의 표현은?
items.why: no matter where는 wherever와 같은 뜻으로 '어디에 가든'이라는 의미예요.

items.q: 'Whenever I see him, I remember my school days.'와 가장 가까운 뜻의 문장은?
o: I remember my school days each time I see him.
I remember my school days only after I met him once.
I remember my school days because I saw him yesterday.
I will remember my school days if I never see him.
items.why: whenever는 '~할 때마다'이므로 each time과 같은 뜻이에요.

items.q:
Although she was tired, she kept working.
이 문장과 가장 가까운 뜻은?
o: Because she was tired, she kept working.
Unless she was tired, she kept working.
Despite being tired, she kept working.
Since she was tired, she stopped working.
items.why: although는 '~이지만'이므로 despite being tired(피곤했는데도)와 같은 뜻이에요.

items.q: 'Wherever she goes, her dog follows.'에서 wherever의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
items.why: wherever는 '~하는 곳은 어디든'이라는 뜻이에요.

items.q: 'However you look at it, the result is the same.'에서 however의 뜻은?
items.why: however + 주어 + 동사는 '어떤 방식으로 ~하든'이라는 뜻이에요. 이어서 말하는 연결어 however(그러나)와 구별해야 해요.

items.q: 'Whatever happens, we will go.'와 가장 가까운 뜻은?
o: We will go if something happens.
We will go before it happens.
We will go because it happens.
We will go in any case.
items.why: whatever happens는 '무슨 일이 일어나든'이라는 뜻이라서 '어떤 경우에도 간다'는 의미가 돼요.

items.q: 'While I like the design, I think the price is too high.'와 가장 가까운 뜻은?
o: I like the design, but I think the price is too high.
I like the design because the price is too high.
I like the design, so the price is too high.
I like the design, and the price is low.
items.why: 문장 앞의 while은 '~이긴 하지만'이라는 양보의 뜻이므로 but과 같은 의미예요.

items.q: 'However hard the test was, Mia passed.'와 가장 가까운 뜻은?
o: The test was easy, so Mia passed.
Mia passed because the test was hard.
The test was very hard, but Mia passed.
Mia failed because the test was hard.
items.why: however hard는 '아무리 어려워도'라는 뜻이므로 시험은 매우 어려웠지만 Mia가 통과했다는 뜻이에요.

items.q: 'The shop stays open whatever the weather.'와 가장 가까운 뜻은?
o: The shop opens only in good weather.
The shop opens in any kind of weather.
The shop opens when the weather changes.
The shop opens after checking the weather.
items.why: whatever the weather는 '날씨가 어떻든'이라는 뜻이라서 어떤 날씨에도 연다는 뜻이에요.

items.q: 'Even if you fail, you can try again.'와 가장 가까운 뜻은?
o: You can try again only if you fail.
Failing does not stop you from trying again.
You will fail, so you can try again.
You must fail before you try again.
items.why: even if는 '실패하더라도'라는 가정의 양보이므로 실패가 다시 시도하는 것을 막지 못한다는 뜻이에요.

items.q:
다음 우리말을 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?
아무리 바빠도 그는 매일 운동한다.
o: However he is busy, he exercises every day.
Although busy, but he exercises every day.
However is he busy, he exercises every day.
However busy he is, he exercises every day.
items.why: '아무리 바빠도'는 however busy he is 어순으로 나타내요.

items.q:
다음 우리말을 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?
누가 오든지 우리는 환영한다.
o: Whoever do come, we welcome them.
items.why: comes의 주어가 되는 '누가 ~하든'은 whoever로 나타내요.

items.q:
다음 우리말을 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?
네가 어디에 있든 나는 너를 생각할 거야.
o: Whenever you are, I will think of you.
Wherever are you, I will think of you.
Wherever you are, I will think of you.
Wherever you are, I will thinking of you.
items.why: '어디에 있든'은 wherever you are이고, will 뒤에는 동사원형을 써요.

items.q:
다음 우리말을 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?
비가 오더라도 경기는 열릴 것이다.
o: Even if it will rain, the game will be held.
Even it rains, the game held will be.
Even if it rains, the game will be held.
If even rains, the game will be held.
items.why: even if절에서는 미래의 일도 현재시제로 쓰고, 주절은 will be held로 나타내요.

items.q:
다음 우리말을 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?
그녀는 어렸지만 매우 용감했다.
o: Though she was young, but she was very brave.
Though she was young, she was very brave.
Despite she was young, she was very brave.
Despite young, she was very brave.
items.why: though가 이끄는 절 뒤에는 but을 함께 쓰지 않고, despite는 절을 이끌 수 없어요.

items.q:
다음 우리말을 영어로 바르게 옮긴 것은?
무엇을 먹든 천천히 먹어라.
o: Whatever you eat it, eat slowly.
items.why: '무엇을 ~하든'은 whatever로 나타내고, eat의 목적어이므로 it을 또 쓰지 않아요.

items.q: 'Whoever breaks the rule will be punished.'에서 whoever의 쓰임으로 알맞은 것은?
items.why: whoever는 'anyone who'처럼 선행사를 포함한 복합관계대명사이고 breaks의 주어 역할을 해요.

items.q: 선택할 수 있는 범위가 두세 개로 정해져 있을 때 어울리는 복합관계사는?
items.why: whichever는 정해진 범위 안에서 '어느 쪽(것)을 ~하든'이라는 뜻을 나타내요.

items.q: 다음 중 괄호로 표시한 whatever절이 '주어' 역할을 하는 명사절인 문장은?
o: [Whatever she bakes], I will eat it.
[Whatever she may bake], I am full.
items.why: '[Whatever she bakes] smells delicious.'에서는 whatever절이 문장의 주어이고, 나머지는 쉼표로 분리된 양보의 부사절이에요.

items.q: 다음 중 양보의 뜻이 없는 문장은?
o: However fast he runs, he cannot catch the bus.
Whenever it rains, the roof leaks.
No matter who calls, do not answer.
items.why: whenever it rains는 '비가 올 때마다'라는 뜻이라 반복되는 때를 나타내고 양보의 의미는 없어요.

items.q: 다음 중 'no matter wh-'로 바꿔 쓸 수 없는 복합관계사절이 있는 문장은?
o: Whatever she cooks, it tastes great.
Whoever calls, I will not answer.
Wherever he goes, he takes a book.
items.why: 'Whatever she cooks tastes great.'의 whatever절은 주어 역할을 하는 명사절이라 no matter what으로 바꿀 수 없어요. 나머지는 양보의 부사절이에요.

items.q: 다음 중 however가 '그러나'라는 뜻의 연결어로 쓰인 문장은?
o: However tired he was, he kept working.
However much you earn, save some.
However hard she tried, she failed.
He was tired; however, he kept working.
items.why: 세미콜론 뒤의 however, 는 앞뒤 문장을 이어 주는 '그러나'이고, 나머지는 '아무리 ~해도'의 부사절이에요.

items.q:
Whenever it rains, I stay home.
문장의 Whenever와 바꿔 쓸 수 있는 표현은?
items.why: whenever는 '~할 때마다'라는 뜻이므로 every time으로 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.

items.q: 다음 중 어순이 올바른 문장은?
o: However you are careful, mistakes can happen.
You are however careful, mistakes can happen.
However careful you are, mistakes can happen.
Careful however are you, mistakes can happen.
items.why: however 바로 뒤에 형용사를 붙이고 그 뒤에 '주어 + 동사'를 써요.

items.q:
A: What should I wear to the party?
B: ___ you wear, you will look great.
items.why: wear의 목적어가 되는 '무엇을 입든'이라는 뜻이므로 whatever가 알맞아요.

items.q:
A: I am so nervous about my speech.
B: ___ nervous you feel, take a deep breath first.
items.why: 형용사 nervous 앞에서 '아무리 긴장되더라도'라는 뜻을 나타내는 말은 however예요.

items.q:
다음 두 문장을 한 문장으로 바르게 연결한 것은?
She was very tired. She finished the race.
o: Because she was very tired, she finished the race.
Unless she was very tired, she finished the race.
So that she was very tired, she finished the race.
Although she was very tired, she finished the race.
items.why: 피곤했다는 사실과 경주를 끝냈다는 내용이 대조되므로 although가 알맞아요.

items.q:
다음 중 어법상 올바른 문장은?
(whoever 절의 동사 일치)
o: Whoever is first in line gets a seat.
Whoever are first in line get a seat.
Whoever is first in line get a seat.
Whoever are first in line gets a seat.
items.why: whoever절은 단수로 취급하므로 절 안의 동사도 is, 주절의 동사도 gets를 써요.

items.q: 'Whichever you choose, you won't regret it.'에서 whichever의 뜻으로 알맞은 것은?
items.why: whichever는 정해진 범위 안에서 '어느 것(쪽)을 ~하든'이라는 뜻이에요.

items.title: The Reading Club
items.text: Our school's reading club meets every Thursday after lunch. Whoever wants to join is welcome, whatever grade they are in. Last month, however, we faced a problem: some members read quickly, whereas others needed more time, so discussions often felt uneven. Our advisor, Ms. Park, suggested a simple rule. Whichever book the group picks, each member reads only one section carefully and then explains it to everyone else. At first, several students worried that they would forget details. Even so, the plan worked well. Now the quiet readers speak confidently, and the fast readers listen more patiently. No matter how busy the week is, nearly everyone comes to the meeting, because it has become the most relaxed part of the school day.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: Why fast readers should avoid group discussions
How a teacher chose the most popular book of the year
A new rule that made a school club run better
What students should bring to a Thursday meeting
qs.why: 새 규칙으로 동아리 토론이 나아졌다는 내용이 글 전체의 중심이에요.

qs.q: What problem did the club face last month?
o: Members read at different speeds, so talks felt uneven.
Too many new students joined and the room became crowded.
The advisor was often absent, so meetings were cancelled.
Members could not agree on how often to meet.
qs.why: 빨리 읽는 사람과 천천히 읽는 사람이 섞여 토론이 고르지 않았다고 했어요.

qs.q: The word "uneven" in the passage is closest in meaning to
qs.why: 문맥상 토론이 한쪽으로 치우쳐 고르지 않았다는 뜻이므로 unbalanced가 알맞아요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the quiet readers?
o: They quit the club soon after the rule began.
They grew more confident under the new rule.
They prefer to read faster than the others.
They were chosen to lead each meeting.
qs.why: 새 규칙 이후 조용한 독자들이 자신 있게 말하게 되었다고 했으므로 자신감이 커졌다고 추론할 수 있어요.

qs.q: In the last sentence, "it" refers to
qs.why: 모임에 나온다고 한 뒤 because it has become ...의 it은 the meeting을 가리켜요.

items.title: Rain at the Cabin
items.text: Hi Dana, I'm writing from the mountain cabin. Although the forecast promised sunshine, it has rained since we arrived. However bad the weather gets, my cousins refuse to stay inside. Whenever the rain eases, they run to the lake with their fishing rods, and whoever catches the first fish gets to choose dinner. So far, nobody has caught anything, yet we keep laughing. Tonight we will cook whatever we can find in the kitchen, probably pasta again. Tomorrow I hope to hike to the old tower, whether it rains or not. I wish you were here. Wherever you spend your holiday, send me a photo! Talk soon, Mina

qs.q: Why is Mina writing to Dana?
o: To share news about her trip so far
To invite Dana to join the cabin trip tomorrow
To complain about the cabin and the food
To ask Dana for help with a fishing game
qs.why: 편지는 산장에서의 여행 상황을 친구에게 전하는 내용이에요.

qs.q: What do Mina's cousins do whenever the rain eases?
o: They cook pasta in the kitchen.
They hike to the old tower.
They take photos of the mountains.
They go fishing at the lake.
qs.why: 비가 잦아들 때마다 낚싯대를 들고 호수로 달려간다고 했어요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the fishing game?
o: No one has won it yet.
The winner must cook every dinner.
It was cancelled because of the rain.
qs.why: 아직 아무도 물고기를 잡지 못했다고 했으므로 이긴 사람이 없어요.

qs.q: How does Mina seem to feel about the trip?
o: Angry that the forecast was wrong
qs.why: 날씨가 나쁜데도 계속 웃고 있다고 했으므로 즐거워하고 있어요.

qs.q: What does Mina ask Dana to do at the end?
o: Send a photo from her holiday
Call her on the phone tonight
qs.why: 마지막에 휴가를 어디서 보내든 사진을 보내 달라고 했어요.

items.title: Phone-Free Dinners
items.text: Many families struggle with phones at the dinner table. Whoever has tried a no-phone rule knows it is harder than it sounds. Although most people agree that talking together is healthy, the urge to check messages is strong. One family in our neighborhood found a clever solution. Whenever dinner begins, everyone drops their phone into a basket by the door. Whoever reaches for it first must wash the dishes. At first, the children complained; however, within two weeks the habit felt natural. Their father says dinners now last twice as long, and nobody minds. No matter how interesting an online message seems, it can wait until dessert is over. The basket, it seems, has become the quietest hero of the house.

qs.q: What is the main point of the passage?
o: Phones should be banned in every public restaurant.
Children complain whenever parents make new rules.
Washing dishes is the best punishment at home.
A basket rule helped one family enjoy dinner.
qs.why: 가족이 바구니 규칙으로 저녁 식사를 즐기게 되었다는 것이 중심 내용이에요.

qs.q: What must the person who reaches for a phone first do?
qs.why: 먼저 휴대전화에 손을 뻗는 사람은 설거지를 해야 한다고 했어요.

qs.q: How does the writer feel about the family's rule?
o: Approving, with a touch of humor
qs.why: 바구니를 '가장 조용한 영웅'이라 부르는 유머러스하고 긍정적인 어조예요.

qs.q: Why did the children stop complaining?
o: The habit soon felt natural to them.
They were given extra dessert each night.
They were allowed to use phones later.
qs.why: 2주 안에 그 습관이 자연스럽게 느껴졌다고 했어요.

qs.q: In the sentence "it can wait until dessert is over," "it" refers to
qs.why: 같은 문장 앞부분의 an online message를 가리켜요.

items.title: Sleep and Study
items.text: Students often believe that staying up late is the best way to prepare for an exam. However, sleep researchers disagree. Whatever you study at night, your brain needs rest to store it. Even if you read the whole textbook twice, a tired memory works poorly the next morning. In a small school project, two groups of students learned the same word list. One group slept eight hours, whereas the other stayed awake all night. The sleepers remembered far more words, no matter how hard the others had tried. Of course, a good plan matters too. Whichever subject is hardest, study it earlier in the day, and keep the last hour before bed calm.

qs.q: What is the main message of the passage?
o: Late-night study is the best exam plan.
Short word lists are easier for students.
Reading a textbook twice wastes time.
qs.why: 충분한 수면이 기억에 도움이 된다는 것이 글의 요지예요.

qs.q: What happened in the school project?
o: Both groups remembered the same number of words.
The group that stayed awake learned faster.
The group that slept remembered more words.
Neither group finished the word list.
qs.why: 잠을 잔 그룹이 훨씬 많은 단어를 기억했다고 했어요.

qs.q: Why does the writer describe the school project?
o: To support the claim about sleep
To show that word lists are boring
To explain how researchers choose students
To warn students about difficult exams
qs.why: 잠이 기억에 중요하다는 주장을 뒷받침하는 사례로 쓰였어요.

qs.q: In the passage, "store" is closest in meaning to
qs.why: 뇌가 공부한 것을 저장한다는 뜻이므로 keep in memory가 알맞아요.

qs.q: According to the writer, when should the hardest subject be studied?
qs.why: 가장 어려운 과목은 낮 시간 일찍 공부하라고 했어요.

items.title: The Lantern Festival
items.text: Every autumn, the village of Haneul holds a lantern festival. Whoever visits that weekend can make a paper lantern at the community hall. The materials are free; visitors need only bring patience. Although the instructions look simple, folding the corners takes practice. Many first-timers produce lanterns that lean to one side, but the volunteers never laugh. They say that a crooked lantern often glows the most warmly. When night falls, the whole street fills with soft light, and whatever worries people brought seem to fade. Regardless of age, everyone walks together with their lanterns toward the river, where the lights are set on the water.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: A school contest for the best paper-folding skills
A river cleaning day organized by local volunteers
A lantern festival that brings people together
A night market selling lights from many countries
qs.why: 마을 등불 축제에서 방문객이 직접 등을 만들고 함께 걷는 이야기예요.

qs.q: What is needed to make a lantern at the hall?
o: Just patience; the materials are free
A small fee paid at the community hall
A ticket bought on the internet
Tools that visitors bring from home
qs.why: 재료는 무료이고 방문객은 인내심만 가져오면 된다고 했어요.

qs.q: In the passage, "crooked" is closest in meaning to
qs.why: 한쪽으로 기울어진 등이라는 설명에서 crooked는 '구부러진, 삐뚤어진'이라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Why do the volunteers not laugh at crooked lanterns?
o: They are too busy to look at the lanterns.
They believe a crooked one can still glow warmly.
They want visitors to make perfect ones next time.
They think the instructions are too difficult.
qs.why: 삐뚤어진 등이 오히려 가장 따뜻하게 빛난다고 말한다고 했어요.

qs.q: What happens to people's worries when night falls?
o: They are written on the lanterns.
They grow bigger along the river.
They are shared with the volunteers.
qs.why: 밤이 되면 사람들의 걱정이 사라지는 것 같다고 했어요.

items.title: A New Bike Lane
items.text: Last year, our town built a bike lane along Main Street, and opinions were divided from the start. Shop owners feared that fewer cars would mean fewer customers, whereas parents welcomed a safer way to ride to school. After six months, the town counted cyclists and shoppers. Whichever result the critics expected, the numbers surprised them: more people stopped at the shops, because bikes are easy to park anywhere. Still, not everyone is satisfied. Drivers complain that traffic moves slowly, however carefully the signals are timed. The town council has promised to review the plan again next spring. Whatever the final decision is, the debate shows how a small change can affect a whole community.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: A bike lane divided opinions in a town.
Shop owners opened a new road for drivers.
Drivers began cycling to avoid traffic jams.
A council cancelled a plan after complaints.
qs.why: 자전거 도로를 둘러싸고 의견이 갈린 마을 이야기예요.

qs.q: Why did shop owners worry at first?
o: They expected bikes to block the shop doors.
They believed parents would stop shopping.
They feared the bike lane would cost too much.
They thought fewer cars meant fewer customers.
qs.why: 차가 줄면 손님도 줄 것이라고 걱정했다고 했어요.

qs.q: Why were the critics surprised by the numbers?
o: Fewer cyclists used the lane than expected.
More people shopped than they expected.
Traffic moved faster than the critics hoped.
The town spent less money than planned.
qs.why: 자전거 때문에 오히려 가게에 들르는 사람이 늘어 비판하던 사람들이 놀랐어요.

qs.q: What do drivers complain about?
o: There are not enough parking spaces.
qs.why: 운전자들은 교통이 느리게 움직인다고 불평해요.

qs.q: What is the purpose of the last sentence?
o: To show how small changes matter
To announce when the plan will end
To blame the council for the argument
To advise people to buy more bicycles
qs.why: 작은 변화가 공동체 전체에 영향을 줄 수 있다는 교훈을 정리하는 문장이에요.

items.title: A Cook's One Rule
items.text: I have one rule in my kitchen: never follow a recipe blindly. Whichever dish I prepare, I taste it at every step. Even if the recipe says to add two spoons of salt, I begin with one. Ingredients differ, and ovens behave differently, so whatever the book says is only a guide. Last week, my pumpkin soup turned out too sweet although I had used exactly the amount written. A pinch of lemon juice saved it. My grandmother used to say that cooking is listening: whoever listens to the food will rarely fail. However skilled you become, the tongue is still the best judge.

qs.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
o: Soup tastes best when it is made with pumpkin.
Grandmothers always know more than recipe books.
Ovens are the most important tool in a kitchen.
Cooks should taste and adjust as they go.
qs.why: 레시피를 맹신하지 말고 맛을 보며 조절하라는 것이 요지예요.

qs.q: What did the writer do when the soup turned out too sweet?
o: Poured in two spoons of salt
Added a pinch of lemon juice
Started the recipe from the beginning
Asked a relative to taste it
qs.why: 레몬즙을 조금 넣어 수프를 살렸다고 했어요.

qs.q: In the passage, "guide" is closest in meaning to
qs.why: 책에 적힌 내용은 따라야 할 명령이 아니라 참고용 조언이라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What does the grandmother's saying "cooking is listening" suggest?
o: Cooks should pay attention to the food.
Cooks should talk to guests while cooking.
Good music makes food taste better.
Recipes must be read aloud before cooking.
qs.why: 음식에 귀를 기울인다는 말은 음식의 상태를 세심히 살피라는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: Why does the writer begin with one spoon of salt even if the recipe says two?
o: Salt is too expensive to use.
qs.why: 재료와 오븐이 저마다 다르기 때문이라고 했어요.

items.title: Locked In
items.text: Jun had promised to finish his report by Friday, but the library was so quiet that he fell asleep over his notes. When he woke up, the lights were dim and the doors were locked. Although he felt nervous, he remembered the guard's advice: whenever something goes wrong, stay calm and look for the exit sign. He found a small side door, however hard it was to open. Pushing with both hands, he finally stepped outside, where the guard was waiting with a flashlight. "Whoever sleeps in the library at closing time becomes famous," the guard joked. Jun laughed, embarrassed but relieved. He still handed in his report on time, whatever excuse his friends expected.

qs.q: What did Jun find right after he woke up?
qs.why: 깨어났을 때 불이 어둑하고 문이 잠겨 있었어요.

qs.q: How did Jun get outside?
o: He asked the guard to unlock the main gate.
He climbed through a library window.
He pushed open a hard side door.
He followed a friend who came to find him.
qs.why: 열기 힘든 작은 옆문을 두 손으로 밀어 열었어요.

qs.q: What did the guard's advice tell Jun to do when something goes wrong?
o: Stay calm and look for the exit sign.
Call the police and wait inside.
Hide behind a bookshelf until morning.
qs.why: 경비원은 침착하게 비상구 표시를 찾으라고 조언했어요.

qs.q: How did Jun feel at the end?
qs.why: 웃으면서도 민망하고 안도했다고 했어요.

qs.q: What can be inferred from the last sentence?
o: Jun lost his report in the library.
Jun's friends helped him write it.
Jun was punished for the delay.
qs.why: 보고서를 제시간에 제출했다고 했으므로 마감을 지켰어요.

items.title: Learning with Apps
items.text: Language apps have changed how people study. Whoever owns a smartphone can practise vocabulary on the bus, and whichever language they choose, thousands of short lessons are ready. Supporters say these apps keep learners motivated through points and daily streaks. Critics, however, point out that tapping on pictures is not the same as holding a conversation. Even though an app can correct spelling instantly, it rarely notices a learner's awkward silence. Teachers therefore suggest combining both methods. Use the app for quick daily review, they say, and speak with real people whenever possible. No matter how many streaks you collect, fluency grows mostly from using the language in real situations.

qs.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
o: Smartphones will soon replace all language teachers.
Language lessons should be free for every learner.
Apps are useful, but real conversation matters too.
Students should avoid learning languages on buses.
qs.why: 앱은 유용하지만 실제 대화도 중요하다는 것이 요지예요.

qs.q: What do critics say about language apps?
o: Tapping on pictures is not a conversation.
They give too few lessons for each language.
They correct spelling too slowly for learners.
They cost much more than a private teacher.
qs.why: 그림을 누르는 것은 대화와 같지 않다고 비판해요.

qs.q: In the passage, "awkward" is closest in meaning to
qs.why: 어색한 침묵을 뜻하므로 uneasy(불편한)가 가장 가까워요.

qs.q: What do teachers suggest?
o: Using an app only for spelling checks
Mixing app practice with real speaking
Replacing speaking classes with daily streaks
Studying alone to avoid awkward silence
qs.why: 앱으로 매일 복습하고 사람들과도 말하라고 제안했어요.

qs.q: Why does the writer mention points and daily streaks?
o: To show that the apps are too difficult
To prove that learners study much less
To show what keeps learners motivated
To compare apps with printed books
qs.why: 지지하는 사람들이 학습 동기를 유지하는 요소로 점수와 연속 학습 기록을 꼽는다고 설명한 부분이에요.

items.title: Saturday at the Shelter
items.text: On Saturday, forty students gave up their morning to clean the local animal shelter. Although the weather was cold, they arrived before eight o'clock, carrying brushes and buckets. Whoever finished a task early was asked to walk the dogs in the yard. "I thought I would hate the scrubbing," said one boy, "but it felt great to help." The manager explained that the shelter depends on volunteers, regardless of how small the help may seem. Even a single hour makes a difference, she said. By noon, the floors were spotless, and the dogs, however shy they had been at first, were wagging their tails at the visitors. The school plans to repeat the event every season.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: Students gave a morning to help a shelter.
A shelter asked for more dogs to be adopted.
Volunteers learned how to train shy animals.
A school opened a new building for pets.
qs.why: 학생들이 아침 시간을 내어 보호소를 청소한 이야기예요.

qs.q: What were students who finished a task early asked to do?
o: Walk the dogs in the yard
qs.why: 일을 일찍 끝낸 학생에게 마당에서 개를 산책시키라고 했어요.

qs.q: What does the boy's comment show?
o: He enjoyed it more than expected.
He wanted to leave before noon.
He felt the work was too hard.
qs.why: 청소가 싫을 줄 알았지만 도와서 기분이 좋았다고 말했어요.

qs.q: What does the manager want people to understand?
o: Only large groups can help a shelter.
Dogs are easier to care for than cats.
qs.why: 아주 작은 도움도 변화를 만든다고 강조했어요.

qs.q: What can be inferred about the dogs?
o: They were all adopted that morning.
They refused to leave the yard.
qs.why: 처음에는 수줍어하던 개들이 정오에는 꼬리를 흔들고 있었으므로 더 친해졌음을 알 수 있어요.

items.title: Playing Slowly
items.text: My violin teacher once told me, "Whatever you play, play it slowly first." I did not understand until my last recital. For weeks I had rushed through the hard passages, hoping speed would hide my mistakes. Whenever I performed in front of my family, the same notes went wrong. Then I followed her advice and practised each bar at half speed, however boring it felt. Slowly, my fingers learned the shape of the music. At the recital, my hands were shaking, but they remembered what to do. I did not play perfectly, whereas the girl before me did. Still, I walked off the stage smiling, because I knew exactly why each note sounded the way it did.

qs.q: What is the passage mainly about?
o: Playing quickly is the secret of good music.
The teacher stopped the writer's lessons.
A recital is easier than practice at home.
Slow practice made the writer play better.
qs.why: 천천히 연습한 덕분에 연주가 나아졌다는 것이 중심 내용이에요.

qs.q: Why did the writer rush through hard parts?
o: To finish before the lesson ended
To save time for other hobbies
qs.why: 속도로 실수를 가리려고 했다고 했어요.

qs.q: In the sentence "they remembered what to do," "they" refers to
qs.why: 떨리던 손이 해야 할 것을 기억했다는 뜻이에요.

qs.q: What does "whereas the girl before me did" tell us?
o: The girl before made many mistakes.
The writer played better than the girl.
The writer and the girl played together.
qs.why: whereas 뒤는 앞사람은 완벽하게 연주했다는 대조를 나타내요.

qs.q: Why was the writer smiling after the recital?
o: The writer had played faster than everyone else.
The writer received a prize from the teacher.
The writer finally finished the final exam.
The writer understood how the music worked.
qs.why: 각 음이 왜 그렇게 들리는지 정확히 알았기 때문이라고 했어요.
